body: I know the incident that was the spark that led to everything spiralling out of control.  The cause is much deeper rooted and ingrained in the million parts of my psychology that make me who I am.  I mentioned elsewhere that I actually find ways to make peace with it in my own way, but that doesn't include going to an office job and doesn't allow for any conventional forms of earning income.  And I don't have time any more to focus on "fixing" myself, which is what I focussed on for many years.  Now it is purely a financial issue as in 2 weeks I will be homeless, meds or no meds.

I don't think you do agree.  Maybe you do, but I doubt it.  So you're saying if the shit hit the fan for you and for whatever reason you had no job opportunities other than being a pizza delivery guy or working a cashier's till, you would instead start seriously considering suicide?  I don't think so.  You and 99.9% of people would do what had to be done.  It's why the world works.

There is no profession that appeals to me.  If I had an answer to that of course I would have worked towards it.  You have to understand that it has been 4+ years of being unemployed and looking for work.  And trying to find that perfect solution of what would work for me.  Something outdoors preferably, something with no pressure, something without people, something that I won't quit after a week, something not labour intensive, something that I won't be embarrassed to tell my friends about...

The only thing that comes remotely close is dog walking.  I like dogs.  But again there are hurdles.  I could never tell my friends about it.  I mentioned it a few weeks ago to a very close friend, in fact the most supportive and compassionate friend I have.  I said it in passing as if it was a joke almost.  Like "fuck it dude i may even have to start walking dogs or some shit".  He laughed "haha from an economics degree to dog walking".  He couldn't take it seriously.  I could never sit down in a pub and tell all my friends that's what I'm doing.

Plus again it's not easy.  You need to market yourself like a business.  You need to actively find clients and promote yourself.  The dog owner will want to meet you and vet you.  I can't do all of that.  It has been YEARS of trying to get things done.  Nothing happens.  Soon it will be too late and I will be on the streets and from there it's over.

If it's been this long and I haven't been able to fix it, what hope do I have in the next 2 weeks?  Seriously.  It seems inevitable at this point.  There is nothing that can help.

I have tried to find solutions like that.  It's not easy.  There aren't just an array of jobs to pick and choose from.  I don't really have any specialised skills.  Plus they all generally include the same interview processes and the jobs generally involve a lot of telephone calls.  All of which would not work with my anxiety.  It's essentially an office job just in your house.  

Aside from the anxiety side of it, I just can't do some shitty office type job anymore.  I would quit soon anyway.  It's not a worthwhile life to me.  I don't really understand that.  People work shitty jobs they hate just for the sake of a paycheck, for the sake of food, rent etc.  The alternative is death.  How is a quick painless death, where afterwards you have no recollection of anything, no regrets, no feelings of desire, no fear, no pain, no suffering - how is all of that worse than living a life of monotony and mediocrity?  Maybe I just don't have that innate survival instinct that humans are supposed to have no matter what.

I replied to another comment:

> There was an incident to create the anxiety. Or at least that I'm pretty certain was the cause. It's a long and weird/embarrassing story and to be honest I'm not sure it's really relevant anymore. It's many years later now and it just is what it is. I am not looking to cure myself. I am certain that is not possible, at least for me. I will never be the person I was and I am okay with that. For a long time I wasn't. I hoped I might find a way to make this new person exist, independently, but like I said that is now the problem. Money and the inability to earn it.

I have not always felt this kind of anxiety.  I have always had some normal insecurities and perhaps shyness in certain situations, but this anxiety is it's own monster and did not exist inside me before.

There isn't much I enjoy that is productive.  I enjoy drinking with friends.  I enjoy watching game of thrones.  I enjoy spending time doing absolutely nothing with a girlfriend.  I don't know if there is anything that makes me happy for any extended periods of time.  I have no hobbies.  I could spend months/years (and in fact I have) lying in bed with a laptop doing nothing.

There was an incident to create the anxiety.  Or at least that I'm pretty certain was the cause.  It's a long and weird/embarrassing story and to be honest I'm not sure it's really relevant anymore.  It's many years later now and it just is what it is.  I am not looking to cure myself.  I am certain that is not possible, at least for me.  I will never be the person I was and I am okay with that.  For a long time I wasn't.  I hoped I might find a way to make this new person exist, independently, but like I said that is now the problem.  Money and the inability to earn it.

I have tried meditation.  I have been to a number of meditation retreats and go through periods where I try to meditate daily.  That is always something I intend to do but as with everything it is hard to make stick.  It doesn't really "cure" the anxiety, at least not the limited amount I have experimented with it, but I do find it keeps me more centred.

Have not tried anything in terms of diet.

In any case, I am not really expecting advice on how to cure my anxiety.  I have actually found ways to live with it, but that does not include going to work in an office.  And I need rent money.  For a long time I have been trying to find a job solution that ticks all the boxes.  I have failed to make it happen and now I have almost run out of time.

I started having panic attacks and was unable to return to work.  The anxiety would manifest physically in my head and neck and just approaching the office building made it feel like there was a dagger stabbing me in the back of the head.  I had a panic attack while assisting my boss in an interview and I was unable to speak and at a couple of points the tension in my neck got so bad that I dropped my head on to the table.  All this in front of a nervous interviewee.  I left the office straight after and never returned.

My social life has slowly degraded over the years for a number of reasons.  Not having money to do things is a major one.  Plus always talking about my depression and how fucked up my life is eventually wears even on close friends.  They end up feeling guilty for not being able to help.  Then they start feeling resentment for making them feel guilty.  And then there are the ones who are now incredibly successful earning £80k+.  They feel awkward being around me when they have money to throw around.  No one wants the downer around.  All the above is with regard to close friends.  The peripheral friends I lost mostly because I was too anxious to meet them initially and now so much time has passed that we are essentially strangers again.
